questions.stem: What does a converging (convex) lens do to parallel rays of light?

options.text: Brings them together to a focal point

questions.explanation: A converging (convex) lens refracts parallel rays of light so they converge (come together) at a point called the principal focus or focal point. The lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges.

questions.stem: What type of image does a converging lens produce when the object is beyond twice the focal length?

options.text: Real, upright, and the same size

questions.explanation: When an object is placed beyond 2F (twice the focal length) from a converging lens, a real, inverted, and diminished image is formed on the other side of the lens. This is the principle used in cameras.
